contexts.text: An aromatic odour as of an embalmed corpse.
What is cadaverous is then smelled as aromatic. AC 1518. HH 449:2. SE 1100.
What spices signify.
Spice = charity.
Spheres which are perceived as odours of spices, etc.
Perfumers, mentioned.
Camels bearing spices ()... Spices, etc. = interior natural truths conjoined with good. Explained.
Spices, etc. = in general, interior truths in the Natural which are from the good there. Explained.
As the Natural is perfected and also amended through such truths, healing is ascribed to spices of this sort. Illustrated.
Aromatics = such things as are of truth from good.
These spices (aromatic wax, and stacte) are purer than resin and honey...
All spices, because sweet-scented, = truths which are from good. Explained.
Spices for the oil of anointing () = the internal truths which are of the inaugurating good; for spices = interior truths, which are the truths of internal good.
The oil was rendered scented by aromatics that it might represent what is grateful... As all the perception of good is through truth, spices were employed, which = interior truths.
Spice = internal truth.
The aromatic of the oil of anointing = what is grateful of internal perception; but the aromatic of the incense, what is grateful of external perception. Explained.
For the incense of spices () = for grateful perception; (for) spices = truths of faith which are grateful because from good. Explained. AC 10199, Explained.
To multiply perfumes () = to multiply incense, by which are signified adorations.
A city of perfumers () = where is the doctrine of interior truth. AE 281:2.
The chief of spice () = what is grateful from interior truths.
(Thus) interior truths, which are grateful, and are signified by spices, are those which are from the good of love and of charity.
Take to thyself chief spices () = from the Word truths with goods, which are gratefully perceived; for spices = truths conjoined with goods, which are grateful.
Aromatic cinnamon and affection of natural truth... is signified grateful perception affection...

All the aromatics of the oil of anointing belong to the celestial class... but those of the incense to the spiritual class... and therefore in the Hebrew these two kinds of spices are from different words... AC 10254:7, Explained. AC 10291, Signified, Explained.
The spice here named = the perception and affection of celestial truth. Illustrated.
Aromatic calamus () = perception and affection of interior truth; (for) aromatic = the perception and affection of it.
Take to thyself fragrant spices () = the affections of truth from good which must be in Divine worship; for spices = perceptions and affections of truth and good.
The incense of spices () = a representative of worship from truths... Spices = truths and their affections.
Spice = Divine truth as to its Perceptive.
An aromatic odour from the sphere of those Angels.
Spices = truths which are grateful because from good. References.
The spices (of the oil of anointing) = the Divine wisdom. Explained.
